name: Reel
text: I’ll start by pulling the latest pending video list from the transcripts queue—filtering for videos with captions marked as "pending" in the last 7 days. Then I’ll run a targeted `youtube-dl --write-auto-sub --sub-lang en --skip-download` on each of the 12 pending video IDs, saving raw .srt/.vtt files to `./pending_transcripts/`. After that, I’ll verify the file count matches the video count and flag any missing captions for manual review. First action: `ls pending_videos/ | wc -l` to confirm the queue size before diving in.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: Hold—before we burn cycles on 12 pending IDs, where’s the proof those "pending" flags aren’t stale cache hits? The transcript queue’s last sync was 5 days ago; if YouTube’s API latency or our own ingestion lagged, we risk re-downloading already-captured captions. Demand the lead show the delta between the queue’s "last checked" timestamp and the videos’ *actual* upload dates—if they’re older than 7 days, we’re chasing ghosts.
